attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter essay, not a quote or paraphrase of anyone else.

semantics.note: The 'cannot do genuinely new things' part is a fair reading of the contrast he draws with 'something new'. It is a flat assertion, but it is a brief aside in a passage about people's motives. No measure or definition is given, so it cannot be tested.

contract.note: The contract fairly says 'repeating other actions' has no plain test. Read as word-for-word copying, it is plainly false; read as recombination, it can't be falsified. He names no theorem. Declining to grade avoids stretching the claim either for or against him.

evidence.note: Jan 2026 report of Tao's account of GPT-5.2 Pro producing a new proof. Whether that counts as 'repeating' depends on a reading he didn't give, so it doesn't settle anything.
Tao's caveat that AI only solves the easy end of open problems. Background for his scepticism; it doesn't define 'repeating' or test it.

Preprint showing narrow formal and empirical limits on small transformers' extrapolation. It is about one specific task, not a general proof about LLMs. The v3 date is unconfirmed, but the paper is from before the evaluation date.

reviews.rationale: The claim is Zitron's own, but its key terms ('repeating other actions', 'something new', 'mathematically restricted') have no testable meaning. The packet shows a new LLM proof (e1) and narrow formal limits (e3). Neither can tell the copying reading from the recombination reading, so the claim is not scored.
